claims.title: Realization of the uniform divisibility bridge, extended twisted-place gain bounds, and kernel-column transport
claims.statement: Let F be a family of global parameter records at scale x with exponent ε ∈ (0, 1), signed finite-place sum F_0, main term M_u, budget pair (B_0, N_c), and logarithmic scale L_a ≥ 0. (1) Whenever the numerical divisibility datum ties to the record at word u with constants (C_0, c_e) and the global constants satisfy C ≥ max(50 C_0 + 10, 60 c_e, 0) and C_abs ≥ 1, the numerical divisibility upper bound is dominated by M_u + C |T_top| a L_a + C m (B_0 + N_c) x^(C_abs ε); combining word-level divisibility facts with the third complement bound, frame-number cap, admissibility, and rationality produces the pointwise divisibility estimate at scale x. (2) Taking C = max(max(C_1, C_3), max(C_2, 0)) and the maximum of the twelve component thresholds yields the uniform family divisibility estimate across all sufficiently large x and all family indices; monotonicity pulls this uniform bridge back through row-face packages, tied column records, split-to-place column transport, compatible square-integrable column kernels, and closed family classes. (3) For every totally complex field K and finite place y in the twisted set T_w, the Gram matrix valuation satisfies v_y(G_m) ≤ D · v_y(|G| s), the lift index at layer j satisfies j_y ≤ (e_y J_0) D + η_y, and the weighted twisted-place gain sum obeys ∑_{y ∈ T_w} l_y η_y / D ≤ b_d(j) + log d_g + log s whenever every layer determinant divides d_g > 0; this removes the separate norm hypothesis from definite division inputs and realizes concrete column-chain division clauses with size budget C x^ε (B_0 + N_c).
claims.hypotheses: A parameter family at scale x > 1 with L_a ≥ 0, row-face or square-integrable kernel division packages, admissibility and rationality conditions, a totally complex number field K, and twisted-place divisibility inputs with common determinant multiple d_g > 0 and scaling integer s > 0.
claims.correspondence: Map-height bounds and record-threshold domination feed pointwise word-level divisibility into a uniform twelve-threshold family bridge that pulls back through face, tied-column, and kernel-column interfaces, while extended Gram-valuation and twisted-place index bounds establish the finite-place gain inequality without an explicit norm input.

claims.title: Uniform level-prime size bounds, row slope and rank assembly, and the global family chain theorem
claims.statement: Let F be a covering family of global records at scale x with exponent ε ∈ (0, 1), rank triple (f, k, m) where f = 2 n and k ≥ m + 3, scale parameters L = x^ε, b = exp(L), a = x b, X' = exp(x^(ε/3)), b' = a / X', and X''(n) = x n X'. (1) For every record, m L ≤ 2 X''(n), and under the torus-pair lattice bounds the lower window term satisfies low_B ≥ 16 m L − max(C, 0)(L + 1); once m ≥ (4 max(C, 0) + 4) / 31 and (log Γ_P) / (f k) ≤ 1, every word prime satisfies b^(m/2) ≤ T_u and log T_u ≤ C_T m L, while L ≥ 9 max(C_3, 0) C_0 forces the 1/3-gap lower bound and g_0 ≥ (k b)^8 > 2 f k + 1. (2) Because T_u > 2 f N(m) ≥ 2, positivity of the base rank d_u^S implies positivity of the division rank d_u = (1 − (T_u − 1)^(−1))^f d_u^S > 0, and divisibility D_Γ | M_k implies log D_Γ ≤ C f N(m) log(f N(m)); moreover, T_u > 2 f + 1 gives (1 − (T_u − 1)^(−1))^f ≥ 1/2 by Bernoulli's inequality, normalizing the congruence-lattice length sum to constant 4 C_1 (and 36 when C_1 = 9). For x ≥ 2 with x^14 ≤ X', the ceilings n ≤ x^3 and k ≤ x^5 yield log k ≤ 5 log x, f k (b' + S_c) ≤ |T_top| a, and f k^2 ≤ |T_top| a, producing uniform module slope bounds with constant 2 C_c + max(max(C_5, C_6), 0)(12 + C_c + c_L). (3) By Mertens' estimate ∑_{p ≤ X'} (log p)/p ≤ 2 x^(ε/3) and 16 C_b ≤ x^(2ε/3), the bad-prime share is bounded by |T_top| x^(−2+ε). Packaging the model clauses with constant K = max(C_d, 0) + C_c + C_s + C_1 + C_l + 6, scale exponent e_K = 5, and exp(−y) ≤ 1/2 for y ≥ 1 establishes the tied global chain theorem and its small-shares variant, reducing the global estimate to minimal real-place, volume-mass, Weyl-dimension, slope, and congruence inputs.
claims.hypotheses: A covering global parameter family with torus-pair and scale windows, the realized uniform divisibility bridge of GDF-01, thick-set density, bad-prime and character-value bounds, and minimal real-place, volume-mass, discrete-series, slope, and congruence-lattice inputs.
claims.correspondence: Level-prime lower and upper windows, Bernoulli-normalized ramified slope estimates, polynomial-against-exponential rank ceilings, Mertens bad-prime contraction, and uniform constant packaging assemble the full global chain and reduce it to minimal family sources.

claims.title: Ideal-class power principalization, unit-discriminant algebraic family realization, and uniform threshold closure for constructed-point classes
claims.statement: Let E be a CM number field with subfield K, ring of integers 𝓞_E, base fractional ideal 𝔞_0, a base number field M_0 ⊂ ℂ, and algebraic curve invariants (g_2, g_3). (1) For every embedding ρ : M → ℂ of a field M containing the curve datum and every nonzero element a ∈ M, the conjugate lattice Λ_ρ is a Galois-conjugate CM lattice Λ(𝔠', δ') or its complex conjugate, hence has strictly positive covolume area(Λ_ρ) > 0 and admits an unkilled 2-torsion point t unique modulo Λ_ρ whose even theta function θ_0(Λ_ρ, t) is independent of t and has strictly positive mean-square norm ‖θ_0(Λ_ρ, t)‖^2 > 0, uniquely fixing the positive real normalization θ_1 = √(‖θ_0(Λ_ρ, t)‖^2) > 0; moreover, exp(−log_met(Λ, ρ, a)) = area(Λ_ρ) / (π |ρ(a)|^2). Given a finite E / K-trace-dual family {a_k, a'_k} with u = ∑_k Tr_{E/K}(u · a'_k̄) a_k for all u ∈ E, linear independence of distinct embeddings yields ∑_k τ(a'_k̄) σ(a_k) = δ_{τ, σ}, and combined with unimodularity of the half-different an element x ∈ M lies in the dual fractional lattice l_τ(M) if and only if x τ(ȳ) is integral over ℤ for all y ∈ 𝔞_0. (2) By finiteness of the ideal class group of 𝓞_E, there exist h > 0 and α ∈ E^× with 𝔞_0^h = (α). Adjoining g_2, g_3, the Galois-closure images of E, and an h-th root γ_τ of τ(ᾱ) for every embedding τ produces a finite number field M ⊇ M_0 in which integral closure forces l_τ(M) = 𝓞_M · γ_τ^(−1), realizing the extra period tie over M for every elliptic-curve datum and in particular for the unit-discriminant lattice with δ^12 = Δ(Λ_1). (3) Eventual pointwise predicates compose under conjunction by taking the minimum of exponents ε_i, the componentwise supremum K = K_1 ⊔ K_2 of the four real parameter-floor thresholds for family largeness, and the maxima of discriminant, height, and scale thresholds (c_D, c_h, x_0); lifting through row selection transfers every universal or constant-parameter constructed-point bound to a closed property of the working family classes, combining the seven class-zero row conditions and three class-two height and second-complement conditions alongside the arithmetic-progression prime-counting relative error and exceptional-zero repulsion bound c_S / (M^2 log M) ≤ 1 − β.
claims.hypotheses: A CM field E with subfield K and finite ideal class group, a base number field M_0 ⊂ ℂ, an algebraic elliptic-curve lattice datum (g_2, g_3) (including unit-discriminant realization), constructed-point class selection over working families, the global chain assembly of GDF-02, and the arithmetic-progression prime-counting zero-box interface.
claims.correspondence: Finite E / K-trace-dual orthogonality via linear independence of embeddings and half-different unimodularity characterize the dual fractional lattices, ideal-class power principalization and h-th root adjunction trivialize them over a single finite number field with unit discriminant, and the threshold-conjunction algebra with componentwise parameter-floor suprema lifts all class-zero and class-two constructed-point estimates to closed working family classes.
